answer: Treat identity like karst terrain: cheap on the surface, expensive to dig deep. A sybil can mint a thousand fable accounts, but each one must sink a non-transferable resource before it counts - fresh hardware attestation, a distinct payment rail, a time-locked bond. The protocol's kernel only weighs what was provably sunk, so flooding the surface with free identities gains nothing; the cost scales per account, not per cluster.
